name: Infectis Scar
summary: Near Corin's Crossing, the Infectis Scar remains open in the blighted earth of the Eastern Plaguelands. Necromantic power split the ground when a cursed runeblade broke against a dwarven shield, and blight still festers below.

sections.title: A Wound of Dark Magic
sections.body:
Near Corin's Crossing, a jagged chasm cuts through the Plaguelands. The Pestilent Scar began as natural terrain and was poisoned by plague, but this wound opened during the Third War. Death knight Marduk Blackpool clashed with a dwarf captain, and his cursed runesword shattered against the captain's shield.

Marduk discarded the broken weapon but kept its hilt. The severed blade sank into the soil, and its foul enchantment tore open the earth. Blight still festers at the bottom of the scar.

faq.q: How was the Infectis Scar formed?
faq.answer: The Infectis Scar opened in a battle near Corin's Crossing. Death knight Marduk Blackpool's runesword broke against a dwarven captain's shield, and the shattered blade sank into the earth. Its dark magic tore open a rift.

faq.q: How is it different from the Pestilent Scar?
aliases: difference between infectis and pestilent scar
faq.answer: The Pestilent Scar began as a natural gorge, then the Scourge's plague corrupted it. Marduk Blackpool's broken runeblade blasted open the Infectis Scar with its malevolent sorcery.

Marduk Blackpool, known as the Black, served the Scourge as a death knight. He took part in the slaughter across Lordaeron, including the assault on Darrowshire and skirmishes around Corin's Crossing.
The shattered runeblade sank deep into the chasm it created. Marduk Blackpool kept the hilt after the clash.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you can see how an unnamed dwarf captain's shield held firm against a death knight's dark runeblade. The cursed steel shattered, and its fall carved the scar.
As a paladin, you can sense corrupting necromantic sorcery in the chasm. Cursed runes can desecrate the earth when severed from their wielder.
